Commentary.Commentary: The target is not a big one and India will back themselves to chase this down! New Zealand need wickets and in heaps. Can they cause an upset?

For New Zealand, a few of their batters got off to starts but none went on to make it into a significant knock. Georgia Plimmer was really goiod but she did not get the support she wanted from the others. Also, there were a few soft dismissals and New Zealand Women Under-19 will know they are well under par.

That is a brilliant bowling performance from India Women Under-19 and they are surely the happier side heading into the break! After electing to bowl, their new ball bowlers were excellent. The key for India was they kept taking wickets when needed and that pushed their opponents onto the back foot. Parshavi Chopra was the pick with three but everybody was excellent and did their job really well.

It is time for the first Semi Final and it is a clash between India and New Zealand. Both topped their table and are unbeaten so far. India are a stronger side on paper but New Zealand do have a lot of quality in their ranks too. This promises to be a cracker. Who will be the first team to make it into the finals?

The Knockouts! We're down to the last three games of this edition's ICC Under 19 Women's T20 World Cup, and in the first semi-final India Women Under-19 will be meeting New Zealand Women Under-19 at the Senwes Park in Potchefstroom. Both teams have emerged quite strong in this tournament and New Zealand, in particular, have been unbeaten thus far. The Indian team has survived a very close group of Super Six where their progress was due to a superior NRR. For the Women in Blue, batting has been a major strength with Shweta Sehrawat and Shafali Verma leaving a massive impact, however, the others have not delivered with the same consistency - something the management will be looking to better in this crunch game. Their bowlers have been quite disciplined throughout and their clinical last outing against Sri Lanka would have given them more confidence. Against them are New Zealand Women Under-19 who have been dominant in every aspect of the game. Their batting has been ruthless, to say the least and it has revolved mainly around Anna Browning and Georgia Plimmer. Their form has been incredible but at the same time, it has not allowed the other batters much exposure. In the last two games, the batting department has stuttered a little but it hasn't impacted the results. They are entering into this knockout after steamrolling Pakistan Women Under-19 and their confidence will be sky-high. Their bowling unit has been contributing to the success equally and that has given New Zealand Women Under-19 an all-round strength. Two teams look nicely matched on paper and let's see which one reaches the finale of this marquee event.
